name: Caring for a parent — hands-free
triggers: what do I ask the doctor tomorrow
boundary: Not medical, legal, or financial advice. A nurse, care manager, or social worker is the right person for decisions; this helps you get organized and ask better questions. Spoken output — say the next step, one at a time.
ask_first: Are you hands-free right now? If so, we'll go one short step at a time and you can say 'next' or 'repeat'.

steps.why: The questions to ask and the things to say so the appointment actually gets your parent what they need.
Every medication, dose, and time — read back plainly, so nothing gets missed or doubled.
Who does what, and how they hear from each other — so you're not the only switchboard.
An honest read on how you're doing, and the one thing to change this week.
Real relief, arranged — who covers, when, and how to accept it without guilt.

done_when: The next appointment is prepared, the medications are straight, the care team knows its roles, and you have relief on the calendar.
